result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.robins_alexander_clustering()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Compute the Robins-Alexander bipartite clustering coefficient of the whole graph. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.robins_alexander_clustering()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Compute the Robins-Alexander bipartite clustering coefficient of the whole graph. title: >- [Graph.robins_alexander_clustering()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Compute the Robins-Alexander bipartite clustering coefficient of the whole graph. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the Robins-Alexander bipartite clustering coefficient of the whole graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L19489-L19598){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.robins_alexander_clustering() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Robins-Alexander clustering](../assets/graphs/robins-alexander-clustering.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The complete bipartite graph K(2,3): a and b on top, each joined to x, y and z below. Every path of length three closes into a square, like a, x, b, y in the accent color. The card counts 3 squares and 12 paths of length three, so the coefficient is 4 times 3 over 12, which is 1.0." width="100%"} Robins and Alexander (2004) measure clustering in two-mode networks (people and events, directors and boards) by counting squares: the fraction of paths of length three that close into a 4-cycle, $4 C_4 / L_3$. A square means two people who share two events, the bipartite counterpart of a triangle, so a high value indicates that co-memberships tend to repeat, as in interlocking boards. Edge direction and parallel edges are ignored. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The coefficient, between 0 and 1 (`0` for graphs with fewer than four nodes or three edges, or without paths of length three). ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} $C_4$ is counted from pairs of nodes at distance two and their number of common neighbors, and $L_3$ by extending every edge both ways. Matches NetworkX's `bipartite.robins_alexander_clustering`. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~latapy_clustering`) : Clustering for each node of a bipartite graph. [](`~butterflies`) : Count the squares each node is part of. [](`~add_bipartite_configuration_model`) : A random bipartite graph with the same degrees. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two people in the same two clubs close a square. Along a chain of clubs, no path of three edges closes: ::: {#50de465f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec square = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("Ana", "Chess"), ("Ana", "Choir"), ("Ben", "Chess"), ("Ben", "Choir")] ) chain = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("Ana", "Chess"), ("Ben", "Chess"), ("Ben", "Choir"), ("Cruz", "Choir")] ) square.robins_alexander_clustering(), chain.robins_alexander_clustering() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (1.0, 0.0) ``` ::: ::: ### Meeting again `davis_southern_women()` links 18 women in a town of the US South in the 1930s to the 14 social events (E1 to E14) each of them attended, and the `bipartite` attribute marks the two sides. Women who met at one event tended to meet at others, and the coefficient is well above that of random attendance, where each woman attends as many events and each event draws as many women as in the data: ::: {#e2e32aab .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} davis = ec.davis_southern_women() women, events = davis.bipartite_sets() attended = [davis.get_degree(n) for n in women] drew = [davis.get_degree(n) for n in events] random = [ ec.Graph() .add_bipartite_configuration_model(attended, drew, seed=s) .robins_alexander_clustering() for s in range(5) ] ( round(davis.robins_alexander_clustering(), 3), [round(c, 3) for c in random], ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (0.468, [0.282, 0.271, 0.355, 0.315, 0.282]) ``` ::: :::
